decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Following a moderation in the pace of the recovery, indicators of economic activity and employment have turned up recently, although the sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic remain weak.
changes.explanation: Economic activity and employment indicators have recently picked up after a period of slower recovery.

changes.quote: Inflation continues to run below 2 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed added this language to explicitly highlight that overall inflation remains under its 2 percent objective.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee expects to maintain an accommodative stance of monetary policy until these outcomes are achieved.

The Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and expects it will be appropriate to maintain this target range until labor market conditions have reached levels consistent with the Committee's assessments of maximum employment and inflation has risen to 2 percent and is on track to moderately exceed 2 percent for some time.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 14.65% APR costs about $61.04 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.63% and moved +1 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.02% would rise by about $1.62 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 6.2%, and employers added an average of 216k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.7% over the past year (February 2021); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 4.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -2 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 0.29%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.15% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Federal Reserve will maintain its current accommodative monetary policy stance until substantial further progress is made toward its goals.
